message:
pagerduty: INC-205678 fired for service private-vpc-controlplane (customer: AcmeCorp). Trigger: control plane heartbeat failures from onprem-agent net-agg-03 in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Pager duty: sanjay (primary on-call). Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-205678 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Automated page posted to #incidents and DM'd <@sanjay>. Auto-escalation in 5m if unacknowledged.

sanjay: acking - jumping in now. I'll gather quick triage and try remote commands.

sanjay: quick summary from control-plane metrics: agent net-agg-03 last heartbeat @ 2056788950, then 3 consecutive missed heartbeats. No routing changes reported from customer side yet.

sanjay: trying SSH to mgmt IP (10.8.2.14) now:

```
ssh ubuntu@10.8.2.14 -i ~/.ssh/acme_onprem.pem
sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager
curl -k https://127.0.0.1:8443/health
```

sanjay: ssh succeeded but agent logs show repeated TLS errors: `level=error msg="tls handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"`. Suspect cert rotation or CA not present on host. Also see many full-disk errors right before agent crashed: `write /var/log/redwood/agent.log: no space left on device`.

david: I'm available, pinging in. If disk is full we should try a safe log rotation/truncate, then restart agent. I can prepare the cleanup commands.

anna: Support FYI - I'm starting customer comms now. Impact summary: 100% of control-plane calls from AcmeCorp's production cluster to Redwood are failing; frontend retries cause timeouts and some user flows are blocked. Marking customer impact: production outage for AcmeCorp, cutting inference traffic.

sanjay: running cleanup per runbook (runbook link: https://go/runbooks/private-agent-disk-cleanup)

```
# from the onprem host
sudo du -sh /var/log/redwood/* | sort -h
sudo rm -f /var/log/redwood/*.gz
sudo truncate -s 0 /var/log/redwood/agent.log
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
```

sanjay: restart attempt 1 -> failed: `Failed to start redwood-agent.service: Unit entered failed state. Journal has been rotated.` Looks like journal dir also hit disk. Running `journalctl --vacuum-size=200M` to free space.

lee: I can run the vacuum command, go ahead and run it, i'll stand by.

sanjay: ran vacuum, freed ~1.2G. Retrying restart...

sanjay: restart succeeded. Agent heartbeat resumed at 2056789098. Control-plane shows agent re-registered, TLS handshake now OK (no cert errors in logs). :white_check_mark: Monitoring for 10m.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation canceled (page acknowledged and resolved).

anna: notified AcmeCorp SRE via their on-call Slack, asked them to confirm any client-side issues. They replied: "seeing transient errors, now dying down, thanks". I'll open a post-incident ticket and coordinate RCA.

david: can you collect the agent logs and config that show the disk/rotation + cert timeline? I'll take lead on technical RCA (possible log rotation misconfiguration + log growth after debug enabled).

sanjay: copying logs to our secure bucket now and creating a gist with sanitized snippets: https://secure.example/acme/INC-205678/logs (internal).

sanjay: quick mitigation notes for runbook update: add `systemctl daemon-reload` step after rotate, and a preflight disk check to detect <2GB free. I'll draft changes.

anna: Customer comms: sent initial incident notification, ETA for next update 30m, will include mitigation steps and timeline.

sanjay: handing off monitoring and follow-up to anna (customer comms) and david (RCA) in 20m. I'll remain available for rollback if anything recurs. :thumbsup:

lee: added a short cron that will run `journalctl --vacuum-size=500M` on problematic hosts as a temporary guard for now (per infra approval).

anna: creating follow-up ticket INC-205678-followup for RCA, runbook updates, and customer postmortem. Tagging @sanjay @david @lee.

sanjay: closing thread here, will update ticket with timestamps and artifacts. Thanks team. :pray:
_note: This file is a synthetic Slack thread for incident coordination around private VPC on-prem agent connectivity and paging.
